content.value_statement: FDA regulatory data is scattered across many openFDA endpoints. This skill helps AI agents query drugs, devices, foods, veterinary products, and substances.
actual_capabilities: Query openFDA drug events, labels, NDC records, enforcement reports, approvals, and shortages.
Query device events, 510(k) clearances, classifications, PMA approvals, UDI records, recalls, and registrations.
Query food adverse events and food enforcement recall records.
Query animal and veterinary adverse events by species, breed, product, and reaction.
Query substance and NSDE data by UNII, CAS number, ingredient, name, and structure.
Use Python helpers for rate limiting, retries, pagination, aggregation, and local response caching.
limitations: Requires internet access to api.fda.gov and can be limited by openFDA rate limits.
An FDA API key is optional, but it is needed for high daily request volume.
openFDA data can be delayed, incomplete, or revised by source systems.
The skill supports research workflows, not clinical, legal, or regulatory decisions by itself.

use_cases.title: Monitor Recalls and Enforcement
use_cases.description: Track FDA drug, device, and food recalls by product, classification, reason, date, and status.

use_cases.title: Compare Safety Signals
use_cases.description: Compare adverse event counts, reaction terms, and serious event patterns across selected products.

use_cases.title: Prototype openFDA Pipelines
use_cases.description: Build repeatable queries with pagination, rate limiting, caching, and endpoint-specific helper methods.

prompt_templates.title: Find Drug Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fda-database skill to find recent FDA adverse events for aspirin. Summarize common reactions and note openFDA data limits.

prompt_templates.title: Review Device Recalls
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fda-database skill to review Class I recalls for insulin pumps. Group results by firm, reason, and recall status.

prompt_templates.title: Build Product Safety Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fda-database skill to build a safety profile for metformin. Include events, serious reports, labels, recalls, and shortages.

prompt_templates.title: Design Surveillance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fda-database skill to design a weekly openFDA surveillance workflow. Include endpoints, query fields, pagination, caching, and validation checks.

output_examples.output: A recall brief with product names, classifications, recall reasons, dates, status, and the openFDA enforcement endpoint used.

output_examples.input: Compare adverse reactions for aspirin and ibuprofen.
output_examples.output: A comparison table in prose that lists top reaction terms, report counts, serious report counts, and data caveats.

output_examples.input: Look up a medical device by product code.
output_examples.output: A device summary with classification, 510(k) context, recall signals, UDI availability, and source endpoint notes.

best_practices: Use specific openFDA field searches and exact counts when comparing terms.
Respect rate limits, cache repeated queries, and use an FDA API key for large workloads.
Verify important findings against FDA source records before using them in decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad wildcard queries when a specific openFDA field is available.
Do not paste private API keys into shared prompts, reports, or committed files.
Do not treat adverse event counts as incidence rates without denominator data and expert review.

faq.question: What FDA data can this skill query?
faq.answer: It covers openFDA datasets for drugs, devices, foods, veterinary products, substances, recalls, labels, approvals, and adverse events.

faq.question: Does this skill require an FDA API key?
faq.answer: No. The API works without a key, but a key allows higher daily request volume.

faq.question: Can this skill make medical recommendations?
faq.answer: No. It supports research and data retrieval. Medical decisions need qualified professional review.

faq.question: Does the skill write files?
faq.answer: Yes. The Python helper can cache openFDA responses in a local cache directory.

faq.question: Does the skill access the internet?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends GET requests to openFDA API endpoints and uses public FDA data.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
